header.stance: 油價回落與現金回購可能性支撐長債

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價下跌、現金回購報導帶動長債反彈

油價回落，加上市場評估政府可能動用現金回購債券的報導，美國長債週一上漲。10年與30年期殖利率各下跌4個基點，至4.70%與5.23%，2年期則維持4.24%。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率各降2個基點，至2.38%與2.32%，名目殖利率降幅由兩者共同貢獻。

報導指向財政部$9,350億現金餘額，並非已宣布的購債計畫。若直接使用現金，就不必每次回購都同步發行國庫券，供給效果可能優於單純以短債換長債。但貝森特隨後未認可這個選項，並表示例行標售將繼續。市場因此是在評估進一步支持的可能性，同時受惠於WTI下跌2.16%至$85.18、布蘭特下跌2.39%至$92.13。

信用基金小幅上漲，個別借款人卻面對不同條件。投資人開始評估AI保證責任，Broadcom債券與CDS因而走弱；SoftBank則規劃日本歷來最大零售債發行。加拿大貿易爭端使當地殖利率大降，Braskem也取得啟動債務重整的支持。美債基準利率降低之際，企業與主權融資風險仍由各自的條款及資金來源決定。

## 財政部現金是可能的資金來源，尚非新承諾

CNBC引述兩名財政部高階官員報導，政府可能動用財政部一般帳戶，也就是TGA，回購較舊、高票息的公債。該帳戶8月20日餘額為$9,350億。Morgan Stanley估計，依營運緩衝標準不同，其中$800億至$2,000億可能被視為超額現金。報導後，10年期殖利率盤中降向4.69%。

這項估計不等於購債授權。財政部自2015年起，保留至少5天支出、或最低$1,500億的現金緩衝，以防無法進入市場融資。RBC的Blake Gwinn認為，動用現金回購的機率很低，網路攻擊風險反而使較厚的緩衝更重要。除非永久降低現金目標，否則回購花掉的資金，日後仍須補回。

被問到是否增加回購時，貝森特表示尚未買進任何債券。他未進一步暗示債務管理將大幅改動，重申例行標售照常，並表示十一月初季度再融資公告前不會調整。先前宣布擴大的10至30年期流動性支持回購，仍自9月9日開始；在宣布操作規模至少加倍前，至11月4日的原時程列有最多$140億。週一並未增加新的金額。

5年期殖利率收低2個基點至4.41%，長端降幅較大，使2年與10年期、2年與30年期利差各縮小4個基點，至46與99個基點。美債成交額較週五增加9.5%至$1.073兆，其中一般附息公債增加4.7%至$8,713億。20年以上成交$1,076億、增加21.6%，10至20年期增加28.4%至$828億。這些是雙向成交、不是淨流入，但顯示價格上漲時交易也更活躍。

這場討論引用的JPMorgan研究指出，2026年第一季長端市場深度已改善約38%，使反覆干預較難完全以流動性不足解釋。Goldman Sachs、Wells Fargo、Societe Generale、Deutsche Bank及Scotiabank策略師則認為，殖利率若要持續下降，仍得仰賴通膨、財政、Fed指引或企業發債減速。

Citadel Securities的Nohshad Shah提出另一個疑慮：壓低殖利率的措施可能削弱匯率，最終提高進口價格。不過，週一並未出現完整的這段傳導。美元指數上漲0.18%至98.98，黃金同時上漲2.47%至$4,738.20，近1週漲幅7.25%。實質殖利率下降有利黃金，財政疑慮也提供持有理由，但美元走強，並不支持把當日市場全數歸納為貨幣貶值交易。

## Broadcom保證責任反映到信用價格，SoftBank轉向零售資金

Broadcom票息5.15%、2031年到期債券的殖利率，八月以來已上升約14個基點；5年期CDS保護成本增加28個基點，幅度高於Oracle與SpaceX的可比變化。市場正在區分不同AI借款人，而不是對整個產業一律降價。

公司正討論逾$600億的晶片融資，預計支應Anthropic等客戶。Broadcom可能保證部分優先擔保債，但條款仍在協商。保證可讓融資載具利用出資支持者較強的信用取得借款；若客戶現金流、擔保品或再融資不如預期，也可能使責任回到保證人。直接持有公司債的投資人，因此需要把這些承諾與一般債務一起評估。

JPMorgan的Tarek Hamid將保證、租約、採購承諾與殘值支持的累積，形容為AI生態系下方的一層槓桿，最終可能達數兆美元。各種義務的順位與被要求履行機率不同；當同一批企業同時供應設備、資助客戶，又支持資產價值，法律上究竟承諾了什麼，就愈來愈重要。

SoftBank計畫發行¥1兆、約$63億的7年期零售債，為日本發行人歷來最大同類交易。預計9月4日定價，初步票息區間4.3%至4.9%。其中¥4,000億將償還九月到期零售債，其餘用於AI投資，包括對OpenAI逾$600億的承諾及資料中心支出。

本次債券預期取得Japan Credit Rating Agency的A評等，但S&P給SoftBank的發行人評等為BB+，低於投資級一級，七月將展望調為穩定。銀行存款成長偏弱，可能限制其承擔信用與7年期久期的意願，使零售投資人需要吸收較大部分。Bloomberg Intelligence預期票息可能落在區間上緣。SoftBank四月與六月已分別募得¥4,180億及¥2,600億；即使完成今年第3次零售發行，資金缺口仍可能超過$200億，後續海外融資機會因而偏高。

美國整體市場仍有可觀容量。八月投資級供給達$1,570億，連續第3個月創下該月份紀錄，主要交易包括Alphabet的$250億，以及AbbVie與Advanced Micro Devices等。JPMorgan Asset Management的Kelsey Berro表示，九月發行預估介於$1,750億至$2,500億，$750億的落差使部位安排較困難；但她也指出，零售需求已超過至少2010年以來任何一年的全年總額。企業今年為資料中心及相關AI投資借入逾$4,100億，目前強勁需求仍能承接，不同借款人則為自身風險付出不同價格。

Nvidia財報前，股票投資人較為審慎。記憶體成本上升，客戶面對明年初交付的AI系統漲價逾15%；Nvidia當日下跌2.9%，Nasdaq 100跌0.97%，半導體指數跌2.70%。財報尚未公布，跌勢並非對已揭露需求的定論。S&P 500跌幅較小，為0.28%，VIX升至15.85。

## 加拿大貿易爭端壓低成長預期，伊朗措施仍缺細節

與美國貿易談判破裂後，加拿大匯債反應劇烈。加幣一度下跌0.7%，至每美元C$1.3851，為G10最弱；2年與10年期殖利率各最多下跌9個基點，至2.95%與3.68%。交換市場反映至隔年七月升息65個基點，低於週五的75個基點。

美國對數百種加拿大產品實施50%關稅，總理Mark Carney承諾自9月8日起，對約$200億美國商品課徵報復關稅。渥太華正準備可能延續至美國期中選舉之後的支持措施；有估計指出，若關稅持續，90,000個加拿大工作可能受威脅。當下利率反應較重視投資與就業受損，而非關稅漲價效果，但匯率貶值與反制措施仍可能在爭端延長時推升通膨。

貝森特另威脅懲罰繼續與伊朗往來的國家，表示川普正向各國領袖提出具體要求及配合期限。不過，公告未附國家或企業層級的詳細措施，油價仍維持跌勢。伊朗里亞爾已跌至每美元204萬的紀錄，對亞洲出貨幾乎枯竭，稀少船貨也由折價轉為每桶約$4溢價。進一步執法可能使油流更緊，但週一價格尚未反映這個結果已經確定。

## 印尼吸引資金回流，土耳其取消緊急融資溢價

外資週四淨買入$6.567億印尼公債，為2019年7月以來最大單日流入，八月累計達$9.3174億。印尼盾本月已升值1.8%，10年期殖利率較六月高點下降52個基點。近期標售投標量為目標的2.65倍，外資投標Rp17.2兆，高於今年平均Rp8.3兆。

資金回流發生在印尼央行維持利率、擴大避險獎勵之後，同時有較低的預算赤字規劃與SRBI標售頻率下降配合。即使相對收益優勢收窄，匯率穩定仍吸引買家回來。

土耳其恢復以37%政策利率進行1週附買回操作，取代三月伊朗戰爭後採用的40%隔夜緊急資金。調整早於預期，在正式政策利率不變下，取消3個百分點的融資溢價。2年期殖利率下跌58個基點，10年期下跌25個基點，銀行股最多上漲4.1%。融資成本下降可改善利差收入，但七月31.8%通膨與央行修正後28%的年底預測，限制進一步正常化空間。

墨西哥資料則支持按兵不動。第二季GDP終值季增1.4%，前季修正為萎縮0.3%，本季也略低於初值1.5%。營建成長4.8%、服務2.3%。八月上半月整體年通膨由3.14%升至3.26%，核心僅由3.95%降至3.93%。Banxico利率為6.5%，成長反彈與服務價格壓力持續，支持維持現狀。

墨西哥也準備最多6檔、3.5至20年期Samurai債，預計8月28日定價，初步討論為TONAR mid-swap之上100至200個基點。即使當季成長改善，評等壓力與美國貿易安排不確定，仍影響這次主權融資。

尚比亞總統Hakainde Hichilema連任後首次本幣標售，投標額比K63億供給高37%。7年期殖利率較六月下降101個基點至14.79%，扭轉前次認購不足，但反對派法律挑戰仍在。Moody's另將巴基斯坦由Caa1升至B3、展望穩定，理由包括存底、財政指標及債務負擔能力改善。外匯存底達$171億，多數美元債上漲；不過評等仍屬投機級，稅收基礎狹窄、外部融資及債務承擔能力也仍薄弱。

## Braskem啟動債務重整，龍光取得法院核准

《O Estado de Sao Paulo》報導，Braskem與主要債權人同意推動庭外重整。公司原本急於在週一期限前取得三分之一支持門檻，現在各方有90天完成條款。鹽礦環境災害、石化價格疲弱及股權交易多次失敗，已造成多年現金壓力，公司六月先取得緊急債權人保護。報導未提供更多申請細節，公司也未立即評論。

Novonor以Braskem持股擔保的未清償貸款共R$210億，貸款人出售債權後，IG4 Capital取得共同控制權。Elliott、Contrarian等債權人曾要求Petrobras提供股本、營運資金或次順位債。程序啟動解決眼前期限，卻不代表新資金由誰提供、條件為何已經談妥。

香港法院核准龍光集團債務安排計畫，使約$75億境外債在逾4年違約協商後得以重整。此前兩家子公司的清盤程序已遭駁回。法律核准有助整合債權人，但中國房價下跌仍威脅營運現金流，其他開發商也曾在完成第一次重整後，仍需第二次重整。

Ivanti的困境更直接反映在業績與貸款價格。第二季營收下降11%至$1.89億，備考調整後EBITDA減少21%至$7,200萬。年度經常性收入下降1%至$7.78億，即使占總營收83%的訂閱及SaaS業務成長10%；約5%的經常性收入來自正在淘汰的產品。

財報後，2029年到期、$18億第一順位擔保定期貸款下跌約8點，至面額36%左右。公司年度利息支出接近$2.8億，新端點管理產品的潛在訂單為$7,100萬，但尚不是已實現營收。評等為CCC、持續消耗現金，S&P也指出違約或困境交換風險，軟體轉型尚未緩解債務負擔。

HYG與JNK當日分別上漲0.11%及0.08%。整體市場小幅走高，同時Braskem債權人仍需爭取新資金、龍光正執行法院核准方案，Ivanti貸款人則重新評估現金流，三者處境明顯不同。

## PCE與Jackson Hole之後，九月融資接著受考驗

8月26日七月PCE與8月28日Warsh的Jackson Hole演說，將提供比回購推測更明確的依據。經濟學家預期核心PCE月增約0.2%。若物價溫和、消費穩定且油價未再跳升，有助維持較低的通膨補償；若價格偏強或政策評估偏鷹，目前持穩於4.24%的2年期殖利率就可能承壓。

財政部9月9日開始操作後，實際回購規模與適用天期將更明確。是否動用TGA仍須決定，之後如何補回現金也會影響供給效果能維持多久。到下次季度再融資公告前，例行標售仍是既定政策；$9,350億餘額與超額現金估計，都還不是購債承諾。

SoftBank的9月4日定價、Broadcom最終保證及順位條款，以及美國九月發債日程，將考驗買家是否更仔細區分或有槓桿。順利發行代表融資管道仍開放，票息與個別風險溢價則會顯示，債權人如何為一般帳面債務以外的承諾收費。

overall_summary.headline: 油價下跌、財政部現金報導帶動長債上漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
2年期維持4.24%。油價下跌，報導也提到財政部可能用現金回購，10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率各降2個基點至2.38%與2.32%。貝森特未認可該選項，例行標售仍不變。

Broadcom八月債券及CDS走弱，潛在保證責任開始反映到信用價格。SoftBank規劃¥1兆零售債，用於再融資與AI承諾。美國投資級需求仍強，Nvidia財報前半導體股卻下跌。

加拿大關稅爭端壓低殖利率與匯率；土耳其取消緊急融資溢價，印尼吸引資金流入。Braskem取得啟動重整的支持，龍光獲法院核准，Ivanti業績則壓迫第一順位貸款價格。
overall_summary.summary: 10年與30年期殖利率各跌4個基點至4.70%與5.23%。油價回落降低通膨補償，市場對財政部可能動用現金餘額買回公債的預期，也支撐長債，但尚非政策承諾。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Lower oil and a cash-buyback report lift long Treasuries

Long Treasuries rallied on Monday as oil fell and investors considered a report that the government could use cash to fund bond repurchases. Ten- and 30-year yields each declined 4 basis points, to 4.70% and 5.23%, while the 2-year held at 4.24%. The 10-year real yield and breakeven each fell 2 basis points, to 2.38% and 2.32%, sharing the move between lower real rates and inflation compensation.

The report concerned Treasury's $935 billion cash balance, not an announced purchase program. Using cash would avoid issuing new bills alongside every repurchase, making the potential supply effect more favorable than simply swapping long debt for short. Bessent later offered no endorsement of that option and said regular auctions would continue. The rally therefore reflected the possibility of further support, alongside WTI's 2.16% fall to $85.18 and Brent's 2.39% decline to $92.13.

Credit funds edged higher, but individual borrowers faced different conditions. Broadcom's bonds and CDS had weakened as investors assessed potential AI guarantees; SoftBank proposed Japan's largest-ever retail bond sale. Canada's trade dispute drove local yields sharply lower, while Braskem secured support to begin its debt rework. The day combined a lower Treasury benchmark with fresh decisions about who would absorb corporate and sovereign financing risk.

## Treasury's cash is a possible funding source, not a new commitment

CNBC reported, citing two senior Treasury officials, that the department could draw on the Treasury General Account for buybacks of older, higher-coupon debt. The account held $935 billion on August 20. Morgan Stanley estimated that $80 billion–$200 billion might be considered excess, depending on the chosen operating buffer. Ten-year yields fell toward 4.69% intraday after the report.

That estimate is not a purchase authorization. Since 2015, Treasury has kept a cushion covering at least five days of expenditures or a minimum of $150 billion against disruption to market access. RBC's Blake Gwinn considered cash-funded purchases very unlikely and argued that cyber risks made a stronger buffer more important. Unless Treasury permanently lowered its cash target, money spent on repurchases would eventually need to be replenished.

Asked about increasing buybacks, Bessent said no bonds had yet been bought. He gave no further signal of a debt-management overhaul, reaffirmed the regular auction program and indicated no changes before the early-November quarterly refunding. The already-announced expansion of 10- to 30-year liquidity-support purchases still begins September 9; the earlier calendar through November 4 had shown up to $14 billion before Treasury said it would at least double operations. Monday supplied no new amount.

Five-year yields closed 2 basis points lower at 4.41%, while the larger long-end gains narrowed 2s10s and 2s30s by 4 basis points each, to 46 and 99. Treasury turnover rose 9.5% from Friday to $1.073 trillion, including $871.3 billion of nominal coupons, up 4.7%. Beyond-20-year securities traded $107.6 billion, up 21.6%; the 10- to 20-year bucket rose 28.4% to $82.8 billion. These are two-way transactions, not net flows, but they show active trading behind the price move.

JPMorgan research cited in the debate found long-end market depth had improved about 38% in the first quarter. That makes it harder to explain repeated intervention solely as a response to poor liquidity. Strategists at Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Societe Generale, Deutsche Bank and Scotiabank argued that lasting yield relief would still depend on inflation, fiscal policy, Fed clarity or slower corporate issuance.

Citadel Securities' Nohshad Shah raised a separate concern: attempts to restrain yields could weaken the currency and eventually lift import prices. Monday did not deliver that whole sequence. The dollar index rose 0.18% to 98.98, while gold gained 2.47% to $4,738.20, up 7.25% over a week. Lower real yields helped gold, and fiscal concerns offered another reason to hold it, but a stronger dollar cautioned against describing the session as a uniform currency-debasement trade.

## Broadcom's guarantees reach its credit pricing; SoftBank turns to retail

Broadcom's 5.15% bonds due in 2031 had risen about 14 basis points in yield during August, while the cost of five-year CDS protection increased 28 basis points, more than comparable moves in Oracle and SpaceX. Investors were differentiating among AI borrowers rather than marking down the whole sector equally.

The company is discussing more than $60 billion of debt for a chip-financing arrangement expected to benefit Anthropic and other customers. Broadcom could guarantee part of a senior secured tranche, although terms remained under negotiation. A guarantee can help the vehicle borrow on the sponsor's stronger credit, but it can also create a claim on that sponsor if customer cash flow, collateral or refinancing disappoints. Direct bondholders have reason to assess those promises alongside ordinary corporate debt.

JPMorgan's Tarek Hamid described the broader accumulation of guarantees, leases, purchase commitments and residual-value support as leverage beneath the AI ecosystem that could eventually run into trillions. The obligations differ in seniority and likelihood of being called. Their growth makes the legal scope of support important, particularly when the same companies supply equipment, finance customers and stand behind asset values.

SoftBank plans a ¥1 trillion, or $6.3 billion, seven-year retail bond—the largest such sale by any Japanese issuer. Pricing is scheduled for September 4, with an indicative coupon of 4.3%–4.9%. It will use ¥400 billion to refinance retail bonds maturing in September and the remainder for AI investment, including commitments above $60 billion to OpenAI and data-center spending.

The proposed issue is expected to receive an A rating from Japan Credit Rating Agency, while S&P rates SoftBank BB+, one notch below investment grade, with an outlook revised to stable in July. Weak deposit growth may limit banks' appetite for the credit and seven-year duration, leaving retail investors to take a large share. Bloomberg Intelligence expects pricing toward the upper end of the range. SoftBank already raised ¥418 billion in April and ¥260 billion in June; even after this third retail sale, its funding gap could exceed $20 billion, leaving offshore borrowing likely.

The wider US market still has substantial capacity. August IG supply reached $157 billion, a third consecutive monthly record, supported by Alphabet's $25 billion issue and deals from AbbVie and Advanced Micro Devices. JPMorgan Asset Management's Kelsey Berro put September expectations at $175 billion–$250 billion. The $75 billion range complicates positioning, but she noted that retail demand had already exceeded every full-year total back to at least 2010. Companies have borrowed more than $410 billion for data centers and related AI investment this year; strong demand has so far met that supply, with borrowers paying different prices for their particular risks.

Equity investors were more cautious before Nvidia's earnings. Nvidia fell 2.9%, Nasdaq 100 lost 0.97% and semiconductors declined 2.70%, as customers faced AI-system price increases above 15% for shipments early next year because of higher memory costs. The results were still ahead, so the decline was not a verdict on reported demand. The S&P 500 slipped a smaller 0.28%, and VIX rose to 15.85.

## Canada's trade dispute lowers growth expectations; Iran measures lack detail

Canada's currency and bonds reacted sharply to the collapse of US trade talks. The loonie fell as much as 0.7% to C$1.3851 per US dollar, the weakest G10 performance. Two- and 10-year yields each fell as much as 9 basis points, to 2.95% and 3.68%. Swaps priced 65 basis points of hikes by the following July, down from 75 on Friday.

US tariffs of 50% took effect on hundreds of Canadian products, and Prime Minister Mark Carney pledged counter-tariffs on about $20 billion of US goods from September 8. Ottawa was preparing support that could extend beyond the US midterm elections; one estimate put 90,000 Canadian jobs at risk if the duties persisted. The immediate rate response favored weaker investment and employment over the tariff price effect. Currency depreciation and retaliation still pose inflation risks if the dispute lasts.

Bessent also threatened penalties against countries continuing to do business with Iran, saying Trump was contacting leaders with specific requests and compliance timelines. No detailed country or company measures accompanied the announcement, and oil retained its decline. Iran's rial had fallen to a record 2.04 million per dollar, shipments to Asia had almost dried up, and scarce cargoes were trading at a premium of about $4 a barrel rather than a discount. Additional enforcement could tighten those flows further, but Monday's prices did not assume that outcome.

## Indonesia attracts inflows; Turkey removes an emergency funding premium

Foreign investors bought a net $656.7 million of Indonesian government bonds on Thursday, the largest daily inflow since July 2019, taking August buying to $931.74 million. The rupiah had gained 1.8% this month and 10-year yields had fallen 52 basis points from June's peak. A recent auction drew bids at 2.65 times the target, with foreign bids of Rp17.2 trillion against a yearly average of Rp8.3 trillion.

The inflows followed Bank Indonesia's hold and expanded hedging incentives, alongside a lower planned deficit and reduced SRBI auction frequency. Currency stability was bringing buyers back even as the yield advantage narrowed.

Turkey resumed one-week repo auctions at its 37% policy rate, replacing the emergency reliance on 40% overnight funding introduced after the Iran war in March. The earlier-than-expected change removed a 3-percentage-point funding premium without cutting the formal policy rate. Two-year yields fell 58 basis points, 10-year yields fell 25, and bank shares rose as much as 4.1%. Cheaper funding can help bank margins, although July inflation of 31.8% and the central bank's revised 28% year-end forecast limit the room for further normalization.

Mexico's data supported a hold. Final second-quarter GDP grew 1.4% from the prior quarter, following a revised 0.3% contraction and slightly below the 1.5% preliminary estimate. Construction grew 4.8% and services 2.3%. Annual headline inflation rose to 3.26% in the first half of August from 3.14%, while core eased only to 3.93% from 3.95%. With Banxico at 6.5%, the rebound and persistent service-price pressure supported leaving rates unchanged.

Mexico is also preparing up to six Samurai tranches, from 3.5 to 20 years, for August 28 pricing. Initial discussions were 100–200 basis points over TONAR mid-swaps. Rating pressure and uncertain US trade arrangements remain relevant to that funding exercise despite the better quarterly growth result.

Zambia's first local-currency auction after President Hakainde Hichilema's election victory drew bids 37% above the K6.3 billion offered. Seven-year yields fell 101 basis points from June to 14.79%, reversing the previous auction shortfall, although an opposition legal challenge remained. Moody's separately upgraded Pakistan to B3 from Caa1 with a stable outlook, citing stronger reserves, fiscal metrics and debt affordability. Reserves reached $17.1 billion and most dollar bonds gained. Pakistan remains speculative grade, with a narrow revenue base and continuing external and debt-affordability weaknesses.

## Braskem starts its debt rework; Logan wins court approval

Braskem reached agreement with key creditors to pursue an out-of-court restructuring, O Estado de Sao Paulo reported. It had been seeking the one-third support threshold before Monday's deadline and now has 90 days to finalize terms. The company had obtained emergency creditor protection in June after years of cash pressure from a salt-mine environmental disaster, weak petrochemical prices and failed ownership transactions. The report supplied no further filing details, and the company did not immediately comment.

IG4 Capital took shared control after lenders sold unpaid loans secured by Novonor's Braskem shares; those loans totaled R$21 billion. Elliott, Contrarian and other creditors had sought equity, working capital or junior debt from Petrobras. Starting the process resolves the immediate procedural deadline, not the question of who will supply fresh capital and on what terms.

A Hong Kong court sanctioned Logan Group's scheme of arrangement, allowing about $7.5 billion of offshore debt to be restructured after more than four years of default negotiations. The decision follows dismissal of winding-up proceedings against two units. Legal approval improves creditor coordination, but falling Chinese home prices continue to threaten operating cash flow. Other developers have needed a second restructuring after completing their first.

Ivanti's problem was more immediately visible in earnings and its loan price. Second-quarter revenue fell 11% to $189 million and pro forma adjusted EBITDA declined 21% to $72 million. Annual recurring revenue slipped 1% to $778 million, despite 10% growth in subscription and SaaS revenue, which represents 83% of the total. About 5% of recurring revenue comes from products being phased out.

The $1.8 billion first-lien term loan due in 2029 fell about 8 points to roughly 36 cents after the results. Annual interest expense is near $280 million, while the pipeline for the new endpoint-management product is $71 million. That pipeline is not realized revenue. With a CCC rating, cash burn and S&P's stated risk of default or distressed exchange, the software transition has not yet relieved the debt burden.

HYG and JNK gained 0.11% and 0.08% on the day. Those modest broad-market gains coexisted with very different outcomes for creditors seeking new capital at Braskem, implementing Logan's court-approved scheme or reassessing Ivanti's cash flow.

## PCE and Jackson Hole precede September's funding tests

July PCE on August 26 and Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole address will give investors firmer evidence than buyback speculation. Economists expect core PCE to rise about 0.2% on the month. A benign result with stable consumption and no renewed oil surge would help sustain lower inflation compensation; firmer prices or a hawkish policy assessment could put the steady 4.24% 2-year yield under pressure.

For Treasury, the September 9 start will establish actual operation sizes and eligible maturities. Any use of the TGA would require a decision, and subsequent cash rebuilding would matter to the lasting supply effect. Regular auctions remain the stated policy through the next refunding. Neither the $935 billion balance nor estimates of excess cash should be treated as committed purchases.

SoftBank's September 4 pricing, Broadcom's eventual guarantee and seniority terms, and the US September calendar will test whether demand is becoming more selective about contingent leverage. Successful placement would preserve funding access, while coupons and issuer risk premiums will show how much creditors charge for promises beyond ordinary balance-sheet debt.
